lessons.title: Daily bite
lessons.objective: You can retrieve one term a day.

payload.prompt: How many tries does a team get to gain 10 yards?

options.text: Three tries
Four tries
Two tries

explanation.correct: Four down tries to gain 10 yards. Gain them and the count resets to first down.
explanation.incorrect: Four tries (downs) to gain 10 yards. That is the whole game.
explanation.sayThisLine: Four tries to go ten yards, that is one set of downs.

payload.prompt: If the offense gains 10 yards, they earn a ___.

explanation.correct: A fresh set of four downs is a first down. The count resets.
explanation.incorrect: Ten yards or more earns a fresh set of four downs, which is called a first down.

payload.prompt: In zone coverage, what do defenders guard?

options.text: One specific receiver wherever he goes
An area of the field
The quarterback only

explanation.correct: Zone coverage: defenders guard areas. Man coverage: defenders follow a receiver.
explanation.incorrect: Zone is areas, man is receivers. If they sit in the zone, receivers can come and go.
explanation.sayThisLine: Zone is where; man is who.

payload.prompt: When fans say 'third and seven,' they mean it is the third ___ and the team needs 7 more ___.

explanation.correct: Down and distance: which down it is and how many yards needed. Third and seven is make-or-break.
explanation.incorrect: Down says which try (1-4). Distance is yards still needed.

lessons.title: Weekly mix
lessons.objective: You can mix terms, scenes and conversation.

statement.speaker: Commentator
statement.text: They got the first down. That keeps the drive alive.

payload.question: What does the commentator mean?

options.text: The offense ran out of tries and the drive is over.
The offense gained 10 yards or more, so they get a fresh set of four tries.
The first play of the game always succeeds.
The clock stopped for a timeout.

payload.translation: Getting a first down means earning a fresh set of downs. The drive continues.

followUps.line: What happens if they do not get the first down?
followUps.why: Understanding the stakes: no first down means turnover on downs (punt or fourth-down decision).

followUps.line: Can you get a first down on fourth down?
followUps.why: Yes, if the offense gains 10 yards on any down, it is a fresh set.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If unsure, first down equals a fresh set of four tries.

payload.prompt: Match each coverage to how it splits the deep field.

pairs.definition: Two safeties split the deep field into halves; corners guard the flats and seams.
Three defenders split the deep field into thirds; a Cover 2 with one safety inside.

explanation.summary: Both use safeties deep, but two divides the field in half while three divides it in thirds.
explanation.sayThisLine: Cover 2 is halves. Cover 3 is thirds.

payload.prompt: Gap assignments tell defenders where to watch for the run. True or false?

scene.alt: Defensive linemen and linebackers standing in their assigned gaps along the line of scrimmage.

explanation.correct: True. Each defender has a gap (A, B, C) to watch. If they lose their gap, the run escapes.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, gap assignments are how the defense organizes itself to stop the run.

statement.speaker: Friend
statement.text: That cornerback got burned deep. He was in single coverage.

payload.question: What is an honest follow-up question here?

options.text: Was it a blown play or was the receiver just faster?
That is the worst corner in the league, he should be cut.
I knew he would get beat there, I could see it coming.
The safety should have rotated over.

payload.translation: A real question shows you listened and want to understand the play, not that you already knew what was going to happen. Asking about the scheme or the circumstances is how you sound like you get it.

followUps.line: How do you tell if it was a scheme problem or a player problem?
followUps.why: Schema problems are about coverage calls; player problems are about execution or talent. Both are legit conversations.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Honest questions beat confident fake analysis. Ask what happened, not declare what you already knew.

payload.prompt: Match the pass-rush concept to what it is.

pairs.definition: Sending more than four pass rushers; usually a linebacker or corner joins the linemen.
Hurrying or hitting the quarterback, whether from a sack, blitz or clean rush.

explanation.summary: Blitz is a call; pressure is the result. Every blitz tries to create pressure, but you can get pressure without blitzing.
explanation.sayThisLine: Blitz is a call. Pressure is what happens.

lessons.title: Sim refresher
lessons.objective: You can re-run a sim on a concept that is fading.

payload.prompt: In Cover 2, the two safeties split the deep field into halves. True or false?

scene.alt: Two safeties lined up deep with corners underneath covering the flats.

explanation.correct: True. Cover 2 splits the field in half with one safety per side. Corners handle the outside receivers.
explanation.incorrect: Yes, that is what Cover 2 is: two safeties split the deep half-field.

payload.prompt: Match the run scheme to its look.

pairs.definition: The back reads blocks and cuts through the first crease; mostly between the tackles.
The back stretches the play sideways, plants and cuts upfield in a lane.

explanation.summary: Inside zone hits straight up. Outside zone bounces it wide then cuts.
explanation.sayThisLine: Inside is up the gut. Outside stretches then cuts.

lessons.title: New season refresher
lessons.objective: You can catch up on this year's rules and storylines.

payload.prompt: In 2026, what changed about the onside kick?

options.text: A team can declare an onside kick at any time, anytime.
Onside kicks were banned entirely.
You can only attempt an onside kick in the fourth quarter.

explanation.correct: 2026 rule: teams may declare an onside kick whenever they choose, not just at the end of games.
explanation.incorrect: The 2026 onside kick rule opened up the play by allowing teams to try one anytime.
explanation.sayThisLine: Onside kicks are no longer surprise plays; a team can call one anytime now.

statement.speaker: Analyst
statement.text: That screen pass had positive EPA. Short plays can still be valuable.

payload.question: What is the analyst saying?

options.text: Short passes are bad because they do not gain many yards.
That play improved the team's expected points compared to what they had before the snap.
Only long passes matter in football.
Yards per play is more important than EPA.

payload.translation: EPA (Expected Points Added) measures whether a play helped the team's chances of scoring, not just the yards gained. A smart short throw can have positive EPA.

followUps.line: Can a run play have positive EPA?
followUps.why: Yes. Any play that improves expected points is positive, whether it is a run, pass, or screen.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: EPA is about value, not just distance. Analysts use it because it explains why short plays matter.

payload.prompt: Tap the zone where the offense is in 'field-goal range.'

diagram.alt: A football field marked with yard lines, showing the field-goal range area near the opponent's goal line.

explanation.correct: Field-goal range is roughly inside the opponent's 35-yard line. A kicker can make most from there.
explanation.incorrect: Field-goal range means close enough to the goal line for a kick to succeed, usually inside the 35.

statement.speaker: Coach
statement.text: Burn a timeout to reset. We need to regroup.

payload.question: What does burning a timeout mean?

options.text: Using one of your three timeouts per half to stop the clock and think.
Wasting a chance to score by using a timeout instead.
The play clock ran out and a penalty was called.
The referee signaled the end of the quarter.

payload.translation: Burning a timeout means calling one of your three timeouts per half to stop the clock, regroup, and avoid a penalty.

followUps.line: When should a team use a timeout?
followUps.why: Strategic moments: avoid delay of game, regroup, ice a kicker, or stop the clock in the two-minute drill.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Timeout = stopping the clock to think. Burning means spending one of your three per half.

payload.prompt: It is fourth and one at midfield. The team is down by three points with eight minutes left. Go for it or punt?

options.label: Go for it
options.consequence: You need a score anyway. Fourth and one is a high-success situation. Modern analytics and your deficit say yes.
considerations: You need points anyway, down three.

options.label: Punt
options.consequence: Field position shifts but you have not forced a turnover. Old-school coaching says this, but you still need to score.
considerations: But you do not make up the deficit by punting.

payload.expertNote: Modern coaches go for it on fourth and one even at midfield, especially when trailing. Short yardage and points needed both say go.
